practiceQuestions.q: The Swadeshi Movement was formally proclaimed on:
practiceQuestions.sol: The Swadeshi Movement was formally proclaimed at a massive protest meeting at Calcutta Town Hall on August 7, 1905.

practiceQuestions.q: The Partition of Bengal was implemented on:
practiceQuestions.sol: The Partition of Bengal was implemented on October 16, 1905, which was observed as a day of mourning throughout Bengal.

practiceQuestions.q: Who announced the Partition of Bengal?
practiceQuestions.sol: Lord Curzon announced the Partition of Bengal on July 20, 1905.

practiceQuestions.q: The Swadeshi Movement is also known as:
practiceQuestions.sol: The Swadeshi Movement is also known as the Vandemataram Movement, named after the song composed by Rabindranath Tagore.

practiceQuestions.q: Who composed the song 'Vandemataram' that became the anthem of the Swadeshi Movement?
practiceQuestions.sol: Rabindranath Tagore composed the song 'Vandemataram' which became the anthem of the Swadeshi Movement.

practiceQuestions.q: The INC officially supported the Swadeshi and Boycott movement at which session?
practiceQuestions.sol: At the Calcutta Session (December 1906) under President Dadabhai Naoroji, the INC officially supported the Swadeshi and Boycott movement.

practiceQuestions.q: Who was the President of INC at the Calcutta Session (1906)?
practiceQuestions.sol: Dadabhai Naoroji was the President of INC at the Calcutta Session (1906) where Swadeshi and Boycott were officially supported.

practiceQuestions.q: The first principal of Bengal National College was:
practiceQuestions.sol: Aurobindo Ghosh was the first principal of Bengal National College, established in 1906 as part of the National Education movement.

practiceQuestions.q: The Partition of Bengal was annulled in:
practiceQuestions.sol: The Partition of Bengal was annulled by King George V at the Delhi Durbar on December 12, 1911.

practiceQuestions.q: Tilak was deported to Mandalay in:
practiceQuestions.sol: Tilak was deported to Mandalay (Burma) in 1908 for 6 years of exile for his extremist writings and speeches.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following was NOT one of the four pillars of the Swadeshi Movement?
practiceQuestions.sol: Satyagraha was NOT a pillar of the Swadeshi Movement. The four pillars were Swadeshi, Swaraj, Boycott, and National Education.

practiceQuestions.q: The Rakhi Bandhan ceremony was introduced during the Swadeshi Movement to promote:
practiceQuestions.sol: The Rakhi Bandhan ceremony was introduced by Rabindranath Tagore to promote Hindu-Muslim unity during the Swadeshi Movement.

practiceQuestions.q: Which festival was started by Tilak to mobilize masses during the Swadeshi era?
practiceQuestions.sol: Tilak started the Ganapati and Shivaji festivals to mobilize masses and spread nationalist sentiment.

practiceQuestions.q: The Swadeshi Movement spread beyond Bengal to which regions?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Swadeshi Movement spread to Maharashtra, Punjab, and Madras Presidency in addition to Bengal.

practiceQuestions.q: The real motive behind the Partition of Bengal was to:
opts: Divide and weaken the nationalist movement
practiceQuestions.sol: The real motive was to divide and weaken the growing nationalist movement in Bengal by dividing Bengalis along religious lines.

practiceQuestions.q: The capital of India was shifted from Calcutta to Delhi in:
practiceQuestions.sol: The capital was shifted from Calcutta to Delhi in 1911, announced at the Delhi Durbar when the Partition of Bengal was annulled.

practiceQuestions.q: Which revolutionary group was associated with the Swadeshi Movement?
practiceQuestions.sol: Anushilan Samiti was a revolutionary group that emerged during the Swadeshi Movement period in Bengal.

practiceQuestions.q: Khudiram Bose and Prafulla Chaki were associated with:
practiceQuestions.sol: Khudiram Bose and Prafulla Chaki were young revolutionaries who emerged during the Swadeshi Movement period.

practiceQuestions.q: The Muzaffarpur bombing case (1908) was related to:
practiceQuestions.sol: The Muzaffarpur bombing case (1908) involved Khudiram Bose and Prafulla Chaki, young revolutionaries of the Swadeshi era.

practiceQuestions.q: Which newspaper was associated with Bipin Chandra Pal?
practiceQuestions.sol: Bipin Chandra Pal edited newspapers like 'Bande Mataram' and 'New India'.

practiceQuestions.q: The newspaper 'Kesari' was associated with:
practiceQuestions.sol: Kesari (Marathi) and Mahratta (English) were newspapers run by Bal Gangadhar Tilak.

practiceQuestions.q: Lala Lajpat Rai was known as:
practiceQuestions.sol: Lala Lajpat Rai was known as the 'Lion of Punjab' for his fearless leadership.

practiceQuestions.q: The Swadeshi Movement began to decline primarily due to:
opts: British repression and arrest of leaders
practiceQuestions.sol: The Swadeshi Movement declined due to severe British repression, arrest of leaders (Tilak deported in 1908), and the Surat Split.

practiceQuestions.q: The Swadeshi Movement was primarily led by:
practiceQuestions.sol: The Swadeshi Movement was primarily led by Extremist leaders like Tilak, Pal, Lajpat Rai, and Aurobindo Ghosh.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following was an economic impact of the Swadeshi Movement?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Swadeshi Movement led to the growth of indigenous industries like textile mills, soap factories, and matchbox factories.

practiceQuestions.q: The Swadeshi Movement is considered significant because it:
opts: Was the first mass-based political movement
practiceQuestions.sol: The Swadeshi Movement was significant as it was the first mass-based political movement in India.

practiceQuestions.q: Gandhi's role in the Swadeshi Movement was:
opts: He was NOT involved (was in South Africa)
practiceQuestions.sol: Gandhi was NOT involved in the Swadeshi Movement as he was still in South Africa at that time.

practiceQuestions.q: The Bengal National College was established in:
practiceQuestions.sol: The Bengal National College was established in 1906 as part of the National Education movement.

practiceQuestions.q: The Swadeshi Movement introduced the concept of:
practiceQuestions.sol: The Swadeshi Movement introduced the concept of economic nationalism through the promotion of Indian goods and boycott of British goods.

practiceQuestions.q: Which Viceroy annulled the Partition of Bengal?
practiceQuestions.sol: King George V announced the annulment of the Partition of Bengal at the Delhi Durbar on December 12, 1911.

practiceQuestions.q: The Swadeshi Movement gave rise to which parallel strand of nationalism?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Swadeshi Movement gave rise to revolutionary terrorism as many young Indians adopted violent methods after the movement's decline.

practiceQuestions.q: The social base of the Swadeshi Movement was primarily:
opts: Urban middle class, students, and professionals
practiceQuestions.sol: The Swadeshi Movement's social base was primarily the urban middle class, students, and professionals.

practiceQuestions.q: The Surat Split (1907) affected the Swadeshi Movement by:
practiceQuestions.sol: The Surat Split weakened the Swadeshi Movement as the division between Moderates and Extremists disrupted the movement's unity.

practiceQuestions.q: The annulment of the Partition of Bengal is considered a partial victory because:
opts: The capital was shifted to Delhi
practiceQuestions.sol: It was a partial victory because while the partition was annulled, the British shifted the capital from Calcutta to Delhi as a compromise.

practiceQuestions.q: The Swadeshi Movement laid the foundation for:
practiceQuestions.sol: The Swadeshi Movement laid the foundation for Gandhian mass movements by introducing methods of mass mobilization and boycott.

practiceQuestions.q: The Muslim League was formed in 1906 with the support of:
practiceQuestions.sol: The Muslim League was formed in 1906 with British support as part of their divide and rule policy.

practiceQuestions.q: The Swadeshi Movement's method of boycott was later adopted by:
practiceQuestions.sol: Gandhi adopted the method of boycott in his Non-Cooperation Movement (1920-22) and other mass movements.

practiceQuestions.q: The song 'Vandemataram' was originally written by:
practiceQuestions.sol: The song 'Vandemataram' was originally written by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay in his novel Anandamath, but it was popularized during the Swadeshi Movement.

practiceQuestions.q: The Swadeshi Movement's emphasis on National Education led to:
opts: Establishment of national schools and colleges
practiceQuestions.sol: The National Education movement led to the establishment of national schools and colleges like Bengal National College.

practiceQuestions.q: The Swadeshi Movement marked the transition from:
practiceQuestions.sol: The Swadeshi Movement marked the transition from Moderate to Extremist politics in the Indian national movement.

practiceQuestions.q: The Swadeshi Movement's impact on Indian industries included:
opts: Textile mills, soap factories, matchbox factories
practiceQuestions.sol: The Swadeshi Movement led to the establishment of textile mills, soap factories, matchbox factories, and swadeshi stores.

mockTestQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Swadeshi Movement:
1. It was triggered by the Partition of Bengal.
2. It was led by Gandhi.
3. It introduced the concept of economic nationalism.
Which is/are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Gandhi was NOT involved in the Swadeshi Movement as he was in South Africa.

mockTestQuestions.q:
Which of the following pairs are correctly matched?
1. Bengal National College - Aurobindo Ghosh
2. Vandemataram song - Rabindranath Tagore
3. Lion of Punjab - Lala Lajpat Rai
mockTestQuestions.sol: All three pairs are correctly matched.

mockTestQuestions.q:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
1. Partition of Bengal
2. Calcutta Session of INC
3. Surat Split
4. Annulment of Partition
mockTestQuestions.sol: Partition of Bengal (1905) -> Calcutta Session (1906) -> Surat Split (1907) -> Annulment of Partition (1911).

mockTestQuestions.q:
Assertion (A): The Swadeshi Movement was the first mass-based political movement in India.
Reason (R): It involved students, women, and common people along with the urban middle class.
opts: Both A and R are true and R explains A
Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
mockTestQuestions.sol: Both are true and R correctly explains A. The Swadeshi Movement was the first to involve masses including students, women, and common people.

mockTestQuestions.q:
Which of the following were methods of the Swadeshi Movement?
1. Boycott of British goods
2. Promotion of Indian industries
3. National Education
4. Armed revolution
mockTestQuestions.sol: Statements 1, 2 and 3 were methods of the Swadeshi Movement. Armed revolution was adopted by revolutionaries as a parallel strand, not as a method of the Swadeshi Movement itself.

mockTestQuestions.q: The Partition of Bengal was annulled in 1911. What else was announced at the same time?
opts: Shift of capital from Calcutta to Delhi
mockTestQuestions.sol: Along with the annulment of the Partition of Bengal, King George V announced the shift of capital from Calcutta to Delhi at the Delhi Durbar.

mockTestQuestions.q:
Consider the following leaders and their regions:
1. Tilak - Maharashtra
2. Bipin Pal - Bengal
3. Lajpat Rai - Punjab
4. Aurobindo - Bengal
How many are correctly matched?
mockTestQuestions.sol: All four leaders are correctly matched with their regions.

mockTestQuestions.q:
The decline of the Swadeshi Movement was caused by:
1. British repression
2. Surat Split
3. Arrest of Tilak
4. Gandhi's call to withdraw
mockTestQuestions.sol: Statements 1, 2 and 3 were causes of the decline. Gandhi did not call for withdrawal as he was not involved in the movement.

mockTestQuestions.q:
The Swadeshi Movement's legacy includes:
1. Concept of Swaraj
2. Economic nationalism
3. Mass mobilization techniques
4. Foundation for Gandhian movements
mockTestQuestions.sol: All four are part of the Swadeshi Movement's legacy. It introduced Swaraj as a goal, economic nationalism, mass mobilization, and laid the foundation for Gandhian movements.

mockTestQuestions.q: The real motive behind the Partition of Bengal was to:
mockTestQuestions.sol: The real motive was to divide and weaken the growing nationalist movement by dividing Bengalis along religious lines.
